heroHeadline: AFRICOM Strikes Push 2026 Airstrike Total Past 83 as US Grants AUSSOM a 12-Month Funding Reprieve
heroSubtitle: US Africa Command disclosed its fifth Somalia airstrike in three weeks on September 17, 2026, hitting an Al-Shabaab weapons warehouse in the Sanaag region roughly 80 miles southwest of Bosaso — AFRICOM's first strike in the north in this cluster and pushing the confirmed 2026 total past 83, on pace to approach 2025's record. Separately, the US told the UN on September 18 it will support a 12-month drawdown of the UN Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) — AUSSOM's roughly $500 million logistics backbone — starting January 2027, rather than the abrupt December 31, 2026 cutoff it had previously threatened; final timelines are to be set during UN Security Council deliberations in December. Security analysts warned the eventual UNSOS shutdown could still trigger AUSSOM's collapse, but Defence Minister Ahmed Moallim Fiqi countered publicly on September 20 that Al-Shabaab 'cannot capture even a single village' even if AUSSOM withdraws. Separately, Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi 'Irro' told US media on September 16, during a Washington visit, that he would not rule out a US or Israeli military base at Berbera in exchange for recognition — an offer Mogadishu rejects as a claim on Somali sovereign territory.
